---

## Katherine McCoy

Katherine McCoy (born October 12, 1945) is an American graphic designer and educator, best known for her work as the co-chair of the graduate Design program for Cranbrook Academy of Art.

### Early Life & Education
McCoy was born Katherine Jane Braden in Decatur, Illinois in 1945. As a student, she first studied interior design at Michigan State University but switched to industrial design, graduating in 1967.

### Career
During her career, McCoy worked with groundbreaking design firm Unimark, Chrysler Corporation, and with Muriel Cooper in the early days of MIT Press while at the Boston design firm Omnigraphics.

In 1971 she founded the practice McCoy & McCoy, Inc. with her husband, Michael McCoy. That same year, she began her career in design education when she was appointed co-chair of the Cranbrook Academy of Art graduate design program alongside Michael.

### Cranbrook Academy of Art
By the 1980s, their sometimes controversial programme had established itself as one of the most innovative in American design education, producing a stream of graduates who went on to make their own mark in the profession.

Katherine and Michael McCoy revised the design program at the Cranbrook Academy of Art: instead of deadlines and conventional exams, they offered experimentation, self-evaluation, and weekly critiques.

### Teaching Philosophy
After coming to Cranbrook, she experimented with various expressive means to communicate through graphic design, other than Swiss style or Modernism, which she found rather limiting. She openly rejected their sterile approach, and she encouraged her students to conduct design experiments that expanded design vocabulary.

### Awards & Honors
In 1983, she was elected to a 2-year term as the president of the IDSA (Industrial Designers Society of America) — not only the first woman but the youngest person to do so.

In 1994, the McCoys were jointly awarded a Chrysler Award for Innovation in Design.

### Later Career
McCoy's career in education was broad, teaching at Cranbrook Academy of Art, Illinois Institute of Technology's Institute of Design, and the Royal College of Art, London.

Since 1997, she and Michael have hosted the High Ground Design Conversation, an annual gathering of design curators, critics, and educators.

---

Katherine McCoy is widely regarded as one of the most influential figures in American graphic design and design education of the 20th century.
